payload.headline: NVIDIA: leadership turmoil deepens the slide; numbers still strong, earnings decide next

summary.thesis: The business is still growing fast and earning a lot of cash, but the price now assumes about 21.4% starting cash-flow growth while leadership, politics and receivables add risk that the 2026-11-17 report has to address.
summary.decision: Hold the long-term position, don't add before earnings, and make no swing trade until the report is out.
summary.act_at: Hold at 162.85; add near 154.19 only after earnings; reassess near 228.42

payload.happening: NVIDIA closed at 162.85, down 2.01% on the day. CNBC reported that the stock is on its longest weekly losing streak since 2012. Media reported Jensen Huang's departure, a Democratic investigation into his dealings with Trump and China, and that the board approached Arm's Rene Haas in its CEO search. Earnings are due on 2026-11-17.
payload.business: The things that drive the business have not weakened in the data so far. Revenue over the last twelve months is 303.0B, up from 165.2B. Sales in the latest quarter rose 105.85% from a year earlier, which is faster than the 73.21% of two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow is 127.0B, up from 72.0B, and the company holds 23.2B more cash than debt. Most of this week's news is about governance and sentiment: who runs the company and how politicians see it. Some of that can reach the business. Huang's reported role in China relations and in AI financing deals could affect access to China and the terms customers get, though these effects show up in no number yet. Two warnings come straight from the filings. Unpaid customer bills rose 127% while sales rose 106%, which can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. And a 65% operating margin is the top of its 5-year range of 16–65%, a level that usually fades. Already-reported demand and the cash pile are not at risk. Future margins, receivables quality and the China channel are.

worth.text: On the usual yardsticks the stock looks cheap. It trades at 20.5 times trailing earnings and 10.3 times next year's expected earnings. Its price-to-sales ratio is 13.0, below the peer median of 17.4 and at the 9.0th percentile of its own 5-year history. The cash-flow model (DCF, which values the company on its future cash) gives 195.92 / 228.42 / 272.22 for bear, base and bull. The stock's own price-to-sales history gives 217.35 to 411.04. The gap between methods comes down to one assumption: how fast free cash flow grows from here. At 162.85 the price implies 21.4% starting growth. Holding the discount rate fixed, 20% growth is worth 154.19 and 30% is worth 224.74. Margins matter as much as growth. If operating margin fell to 48%, the value would drop to 115.89, and at 32% it would drop to 77.58. My range is 154.19 to 228.42. The low end is below today's price because the margin peak and receivables warning keep me from fully trusting the higher-growth cases.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing 20–30% a year and operating margin stays near today's 65% instead of falling toward 48%.

bull: Latest-quarter sales growth sped up to 105.85% from 73.21% two quarters earlier, and the operating margin rose to 65.21% from 58.09%.
The stock trades at only 10.3 times next year's expected EPS of 15.85, and that estimate rose 23.6% over 90 days.
Price-to-sales of 13.0 is below the peer median of 17.4 and at the 9.0th percentile of its own 5-year range, while the business keeps quality grade A.
bear: Unpaid customer bills rose 127% against sales growth of 106%, which suggests sales may have been pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly.
A 65% operating margin is the top of the 5-year 16–65% range; at 48% the cash-flow value falls to 115.89.

Leadership is unsettled: the CEO's departure, a political investigation and a CEO search have been reported, insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans, and the stock is in a downtrend below its 50-day average of 214.63.

levels.what: Today's close. It sits inside the fair-value range and implies 21.4% starting cash-flow growth. That supports holding, but leadership is unclear and earnings are four days away, so it does not justify adding.
Value at 20% starting growth, the low end of the range. Add here only after the 2026-11-17 report shows margins near 65% and receivables growing in line with sales.
Base-case DCF value. Near this price the valuation upside is used up, so reassess and consider trimming.

longterm.why: The business numbers and the automated rule ('Buy now') support owning the stock. The committee's 'Hold', the reported leadership upheaval and an earnings report that can gap the price argue against adding now.

swing.why: The stock is in a downtrend with no support level listed below it, and resistance sits just overhead at 163.9–169.14. Earnings fall inside any swing window. Options price a 10.4% move by 2026-11-20, against an ATR (average daily range) of 9.98, so the report can jump past any stop.

decision.timing: Nothing changes before the 2026-11-17 report. Implied volatility of 83.2 against 54.0 realized (1.54x) shows the market is pricing a large move, so act only after the report shows margins, receivables and whether this quarter reached the 108.8B revenue estimate.

change_mind: If the 2026-11-17 report shows operating margin falling back below 58.09% or EPS under the 2.26 low estimate, I would move from hold to trim, because the margin-peak risk would be playing out (value at 48% margin: 115.89).
If the report shows revenue at or above the 108.8B estimate with margin near 65% and receivables no longer growing faster than sales, I would move to add at or below 154.19.
If the stock closes above the 163.9–169.14 resistance zone after earnings, the case for a swing entry reopens, using the 169.91–175.15 zone (5 touches) as the next test.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold. The stock fell another 2.01% to 162.85, and reports of a CEO search (Arm's Rene Haas approached) confirm leadership is unsettled with the 2026-11-17 earnings still ahead.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
